newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Natl Bank plans CD programme end November.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Natl Bank plans CD programme end November.

text.p: The Belgian National Bank (BNB) plans to issue certificate of deposits in a rolling programme starting around November 25, traders said on Tuesday.
A senior official in the central bank confirmed it was in discussions with several primary dealers in Belgian government debt about such a programme but declined to give details.

Traders said the highly unusual issue was seen as a way for the central bank to sterilise the impact on the money market of its already announced plan to transfer some 230 billion Belgian francs to the Belgian Treasury.
The government said in its 1997 budget it would use the funds, the product of national bank gold sales, to reduce its debt to 127 percent of gross domestic product.

"This forms part of the global operation (to reduce the debt) that has been announced," the central bank official said. "Before launching the operation we had to wait for the legislation to be published. This happened on November 15."

"If they just did a straight transfer and gave the money to the Treasury it would be creating money and the Treasury would have to put it into the banking system. The impact on the money market would be huge. This way it will be neutral," one trader said.
He said the BNB planned a series of revolving credits, issued in several tranches.
Another trader said the BNB was discussing the possibility of two-year, floating rate paper.
